items.question_text:
You have historical data covering the last three years in BigQuery and a data pipeline that delivers new data to BigQuery daily. You have noticed that when the
Data Science team runs a query filtered on a date column and limited to 30`"90 days of data, the query scans the entire table. You also noticed that your bill is increasing more quickly than you expected. You want to resolve the issue as cost-effectively as possible while maintaining the ability to conduct SQL queries.
What should you do?
items.solution_text:
BigQuery charges based on the amount of data scanned per query. Without partitioning, filters on date columns still trigger full table scans across all three years of data, leading to high costs.
By partitioning the table by a TIMESTAMP or DATE column (Option A), BigQuery can perform partition pruning, scanning only the specific partitions relevant to the 30–90 day query window. This significantly reduces scan volume and cost while maintaining standard SQL query capabilities.

choices.text: Re-create the tables using DDL. Partition the tables by a column containing a TIMESTAMP or DATE Type.
Recommend that the Data Science team export the table to a CSV file on Cloud Storage and use Cloud Datalab to explore the data by reading the files directly.
Modify your pipeline to maintain the last 30—90 days of data in one table and the longer history in a different table to minimize full table scans over the entire history.
Write an Apache Beam pipeline that creates a BigQuery table per day. Recommend that the Data Science team use wildcards on the table name suffixes to select the data they need.

items.question_text: You operate a logistics company, and you want to improve event delivery reliability for vehicle-based sensors. You operate small data centers around the world to capture these events, but leased lines that provide connectivity from your event collection infrastructure to your event processing infrastructure are unreliable, with unpredictable latency. You want to address this issue in the most cost-effective way. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Cloud Pub/Sub acts as a highly reliable, durable buffer that decouples data production from consumption, absorbing the unpredictable latency and unreliability of the leased lines. It is significantly more cost-effective than establishing dedicated Cloud Interconnect connections for multiple global data centers or managing distributed Kafka clusters on-premises.

choices.text: Deploy small Kafka clusters in your data centers to buffer events.
Have the data acquisition devices publish data to Cloud Pub/Sub.
Establish a Cloud Interconnect between all remote data centers and Google.
Write a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that aggregates all data in session windows.

items.question_text: You are a retailer that wants to integrate your online sales capabilities with different in-home assistants, such as Google Home. You need to interpret customer voice commands and issue an order to the backend systems. Which solutions should you choose?
items.solution_text:
Dialogflow Enterprise Edition is the correct choice because it provides an end-to-end conversational interface solution that handles both speech recognition and natural language understanding (intent detection).
While Speech-to-Text API only converts audio to text, Dialogflow interprets the meaning of that text to trigger specific backend actions, such as issuing an order.
This makes it suitable for integrating with smart home assistants like Google Home to process voice commands effectively.

choices.text: Speech-to-Text API
Cloud Natural Language API
Dialogflow Enterprise Edition
AutoML Natural Language

items.question_text: Your company has a hybrid cloud initiative. You have a complex data pipeline that moves data between cloud provider services and leverages services from each of the cloud providers. Which cloud-native service should you use to orchestrate the entire pipeline?
items.solution_text:
Cloud Composer is a managed workflow orchestration service built on Apache Airflow, specifically designed to author, schedule, and monitor complex data pipelines that span across multiple clouds and on-premises environments.

Unlike Cloud Dataflow (streaming/batch processing), Dataproc (Spark/Hadoop clusters), or Dataprep (data preparation), Cloud Composer provides the necessary abstraction layer to orchestrate tasks distributed across different cloud provider services.

choices.text: Cloud Dataflow
Cloud Composer
Cloud Dataprep
Cloud Dataproc

items.question_text: You use a dataset in BigQuery for analysis. You want to provide third-party companies with access to the same dataset. You need to keep the costs of data sharing low and ensure that the data is current. Which solution should you choose?
items.solution_text:
BigQuery Analytics Hub is the designated service for sharing data across project or organizational boundaries while maintaining data currency without replication costs.
It allows publishers to share datasets and views where subscribers query the live source data, ensuring low storage and egress costs compared to exporting or copying data.

choices.text: Use Analytics Hub to control data access, and provide third party companies with access to the dataset.
Use Cloud Scheduler to export the data on a regular basis to Cloud Storage, and provide third-party companies with access to the bucket.
Create a separate dataset in BigQuery that contains the relevant data to share, and provide third-party companies with access to the new dataset.
Create a Dataflow job that reads the data in frequent time intervals, and writes it to the relevant BigQuery dataset or Cloud Storage bucket for third-party companies to use.
